newsitem.title: USA: U.S. group to provide $1 billion for Russian telecoms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group to provide $1 billion for Russian telecoms.

text.p: Russia Telecom Investors Fund, a New York-based investment company, said Tuesday it will provide up to $1 billion in capital over the next five years to modernise Russia's telecommunication system using the latest wireless technology.

The Fund was formed in 1996 by Americas Partners to invest in wireless telephone, interactive data and video systems that will address Russia's telephone line backlog and a wait of up to 10 years for a private telephone line in Russia.

The new wireless technology, which is in its infancy in the United States, provides high-definition television, telephone and high-speed computer services via a box that resembles a cable TV control box. Consumers will get just one monthly bill.

"The Russian government is actively supporting (the new technology) as a low cost, wireless alternative to spending $40 billion upgrading the country's existing infrastructure," said Joseph Bernstein, chairman of Russia Telecom Investors Fund.

The investments will be made through CellularVision of Russia, a joint venture involving the fund, the Russian Ministry of Telecommunication, the Moscow city government and CellularVision Technologies and Telecommunications L.P.

The venture has a strategic alliance with AO Svyazinvest, the holding company for Russia's interests in 85 regional and local public network telephone operators, it said. Svyazinvest will market the wireless technology via its network.
The venture also has strategic partnerships with U.S. carriers to operate the systems, said Bernstein, who is also president and chief executive of Americas Partners.
Russia Telecom Investors Fund is negotiating with underwriters to raise funds to finance the investment through debt and equity offerings, he said.
